title: Counting product tuples bad in some coordinate
statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set, and for each $i \in \iota$ let $\beta_i$ be a finite set equipped with a predicate $\mathrm{Bad}_i$ singling out its "bad" elements. Fix a natural number $C$, and suppose that for every coordinate $i$ the bad elements are sufficiently rare, in the sense that
\[
\abs{\{\, b \in \beta_i : \mathrm{Bad}_i(b) \,\}}\cdot C \;\le\; \abs{\beta_i}.
\]
Then, among all dependent tuples $f$ in the product $\prod_{i \in \iota} \beta_i$, those that are bad in at least one coordinate satisfy
\[
\abs{\{\, f \in \textstyle\prod_{i \in \iota}\beta_i : \exists\, i,\ \mathrm{Bad}_i(f_i) \,\}}\cdot C \;\le\; \abs{\iota}\cdot\Bigl\lvert\textstyle\prod_{i \in \iota}\beta_i\Bigr\rvert.
\]
hypotheses_covered: a predicate Bad_i on each β_i
for each i, (number of bad elements of β_i) · C ≤ |β_i|
replaced:
Given for each coordinate $i$ a decidable predicate $\mathrm{Bad}_i$ on $\beta_i$ with
$\abs{\{b : \mathrm{Bad}_i(b)\}} \cdot C \le \abs{\beta_i}$, the number of dependent functions bad
at some coordinate obeys
\[
\abs{\{f : \exists i,\ \mathrm{Bad}_i(f_i)\}} \cdot C \;\le\; \abs{\iota} \cdot \abs{(i : \iota) \to \beta_i}.
\]
